title: Copyright, royalties and unpaid London records
summary: He argues that musicians deserve royalties and describes unpaid songs on his London record.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: And when a guy go out and give an assignment to go write...to write and assignment, they more than likely, if he has any brains, will give him some money to get picture rights, or to get the right to use the name, something...and I just don't think that people should use your material like that in the public domain. If that's the case, then why do we have the copyright laws? Why do we have, you know what I mean, laws of patent offices? And why do we have...so that you can restrain a person from using your material, you know. And I think every person has a right to some kind of royalty or some money for that that he create or participate in.
But most people...you see their name? I just played a record for you that I made in London and I wrote three or four

of the songs played on the record, and I didn't get any royalties. And it's just hard to get them. You just don't know how to find a............ I asked a man last year...I asked Keith Smith. "Hey Keith, what about the royalties on the record I made?" He says, "Forget about it." I don't know what he meant by that, you see. But rather than have, you know, a slaughter on Tenth Avenue, you know, you just let it go. You figure if a guy got nerve enough to just take your material and you looking right at him, then what can you do?
